text: Make sure it's very clear to use the skill on every prompt. So every time I send a new message, that skill is invoked. It re-reads. So maybe the every prompt skill itself should be kept minimal. If there are lengthy instructions, if we need sub skills essentially, then you can have additional readmes in the skill. The every prompt skill could identify any number of sub readmes and give an overview of when you would need to use it, and then just say load this file and read it if you need to do this or this. Those could be on every task or decision or whatever. So we could have different types of sub skills there. But the idea is that if it's loading this on every single prompt, we don't want to overload the skill with unnecessary detail. The general idea is that first, every prompt verbatim goes to the master assistant. And maybe we create a separate skill called master assistant, maybe it can be a sub skill, I don't care about that. The master assistant is going to just supervise, overlook what's going on and be aware of what's going on. If the fast assistant needs feedback, he can ask the master assistant. The master assistant can automatically reply, I suppose. We don't want it to do a bunch of work. It's really just there to give feedback, to give opinions, like don't forget to do this, I don't think you should be doing that that way, whatever. And the master assistant should probably document on some page somewhere that whole process and how it's going. Maybe the master assistant could also be the skill auditor, the system auditor, because that would be a good role for him, to pay attention to everything and think about the design of the system and whether it's working.
